messages:
ryan: Kicking off a RoPE variant sweep summary thread — ran linear / NTK / YARN across Llama-70B, Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8x8, and Qwen-7B at 2k/8k/32k/64k/128k. TL;DR: Mixtral NTK shows perplexity cliffs after ~48k, kernel fallback + KV thrash causing 2-3x latency regressions. Sharing quick outputs and profiling notes below.

sasha: Nice. Do you have the perf numbers (latency/tokens/s/ppx) per seq len?

ryan: Pasted small extract from perf-ci run:```
model,variant,seq,lat_ms,tokens_per_s,perplexity
Llama-70B,linear,8192,210,480,12.3
Llama-70B,NTK,65536,1180,88,13.1
Mixtral-8x8,NTK,49152,920,110,24.8  <-- cliff starts around here
Mixtral-8x8,linear,49152,420,240,22.1
Qwen-7B,YARN,131072,3200,30,18.5
Mistral-7B,linear,32768,360,280,15.0
```
(These are median p50 from 5 runs, small jitter).

maria: From profiling: for Mixtral NTK >48k we hit kernel workspace limit and runtime switches from fused_attn_v2 -> fallback_matmul, which doubles CUDA mem copies. Also KV cache read amplification goes up (more scattered reads per step).

jen: Did you see changes in head/kv dims sensitivity? I remember Mixtral's head dim is higher relative to kv projection which can interact with RoPE scaling.

derek: Yep. Quick micro-bench: reducing head_kv_dim by 0.75 (simulated) recovered ~20% latency and smoothed perplexity slope for NTK at 64k, but that requires a model-level change. Not feasible in prod short-term.

ryan: Kernel selection trace snippet:```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] select_kernel: fused_attn_v2 (seq<=46080)
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] select_kernel: fallback_matmul (seq>46080) // workspace bytes exceeded
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] kv_cache: read_ops_per_token: 1.02 -> 1.68
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] batching: effective_batch size drop due to token churn: 128->72
```
This explains both latency and tokens/s drop.

maria: Other weirdness: Qwen YARN was stable up to 128k in ppx, but latency still spikes because attention kernel uses tiling that causes excessive shared mem thrash on A100 gen1. We should prefer chunked KV caching for >64k there.

jen: From quality POV: Mixtral NTK produces short-term hallucination increase (BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxy goes down) after the ppx cliff; linear RoPE maintains quality but with slightly worse math boundary behaviors. So there is a quality vs long-range stability trade.

derek: Suggested mitigations: 1) runtime: add kernel hint to prefer matmul-fused if head_kv_dim > threshold; 2) batching heuristics: clamp effective batch growth for long-context requests so we don't over-subscribe workspace; 3) KV: implement read-prefetch + chunked writes.

ryan: Implemented quick patch on a branch: runtime now logs kernel_reason and forces fused_attn_v2 for Mixtral when seq>48k only if kv_head_dim_ratio<1.2. Test run shows latency down 30% for 48-64k NTK cases, ppx unchanged. Need broader sweep.

perf-ci-bot: Perf CI results posted: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/rope-sweep/1867001234 (summary + raw profiles). :white_check_mark:

maria: Proposal for safe ranges (initial, conservative):
- Llama-70B: linear <= 32k, NTK <= 64k (but watch kernel fallback)
- Mixtral-8x8: linear <= 48k, NTK <= 48k (NTK above this risky unless model changes)
- Mistral-7B: linear <= 64k, NTK <= 32k
- Qwen-7B: YARN <= 128k but runtime kernel prefs required for A100 gen1
These are conservative and per-hardware.

jen: Agree. We should encode these as model->variant->safe_seq in the model catalog so orchestration can route or reject long requests, and attach a quality SLO flag.

ryan: Action items: 1) eng-runtime to land kernel_reason logging + hint (derek) 2) perf team to run full grid on dedicated infra w/ new heuristics (perf-ci-bot queued) 3) product to add model safe ranges + SLOs in catalog (paging @pm). Anyone object?

sasha: No objections. I'll draft a short runbook for on-call: how to triage RoPE-induced regressions (kernel fallback, KV IO spike, ppx cliff).

derek: I'll open the PR for kernel hint today and attach microbench numbers.

ryan: Thanks all. If you want the raw csvs I uploaded them to /mnt/perf/rope_sweep/1867001234/*.csv — ping me and I'll share access.
